risks.title: Sensitive data is entered into a tool that is not approved for it
risks.description: People paste protected or restricted data into a tool whose approval covers only less sensitive data.
risks.treatment: Name the classes of data the tool may be used with where people see it, and check a sample of use.

risks.title: A supplier trains on what is entered
risks.description: Inputs are kept by the supplier and used to train its models, so they may surface in outputs given to others.
risks.treatment: Use an agreement that forbids training on inputs, and turn off history where the tool allows.

risks.title: People can be identified from data that was meant to be de-identified
risks.description: A model or its outputs make it possible to link de-identified records back to individuals.
risks.treatment: Test for re-identification before release, and limit who can query the model.

risks.title: A model reproduces records it was trained on
risks.description: A model trained or fine-tuned on sensitive data repeats parts of it when prompted.
risks.treatment: Treat the model as being as sensitive as its training data, and keep it where that data may be kept.

risks.title: Data is used outside the terms it was given under
risks.description: Data provided under a data use agreement or consent is used for a purpose those terms do not cover.
risks.treatment: Record the terms with the dataset, and check each new use against them.

risks.title: Inputs or outputs are kept longer than allowed
risks.description: Prompts, transcripts, or outputs stay with a supplier or in logs past the period the organization permits.
risks.treatment: Set retention in the tool, and confirm it with the supplier in writing.

risks.title: Output that reads well and is wrong is relied on
risks.description: A fluent, confident answer is taken as correct without being checked against a source.
risks.treatment: Require a named person to check outputs against the source before they are used.

risks.title: Citations or facts are invented
risks.description: The tool supplies references, figures, or quotations that do not exist.
risks.treatment: Verify every reference and figure before it is included anywhere.

risks.title: Performance falls after the model or the data changes
risks.description: A supplier updates a model, or the data it sees shifts, and results that were validated no longer hold.
risks.treatment: Pin versions where possible, and re-run a validation set on a schedule and after any change.

risks.title: A model is used on people or data it was not validated for
risks.description: Performance measured on one population or instrument is assumed to carry over to another.
risks.treatment: State the population the validation covers, and test before extending the use.

risks.title: Errors go unnoticed because nobody is measuring
risks.description: No error rate is tracked, so a slow decline in quality is not seen.
risks.treatment: Sample outputs on a schedule and record the error rate.

risks.title: The tool works less well for some groups
risks.description: Accuracy differs by sex, age, ancestry, language, or disability, and decisions built on it carry that difference.
risks.treatment: Measure performance by group before use, and state the limits where the output is used.

risks.title: A person is affected by a decision they cannot question
risks.description: Someone is ranked, scored, or refused on the strength of an output, with no way to ask for a person to look again.
risks.treatment: Give affected people a route to a human review, and tell them it exists.

risks.title: People do not know AI was involved
risks.description: Participants, patients, applicants, or readers are not told that AI shaped what they received.
risks.treatment: Say so where the output is delivered, in plain words.

risks.title: Consent does not cover this use of the data
risks.description: Participants agreed to a study, not to their data being used to train or prompt an AI system.
risks.treatment: Check the consent wording with the ethics committee before use.

risks.title: Output is offensive, unsafe, or distressing
risks.description: The tool produces content that could harm or distress the person who reads it.
risks.treatment: Filter outputs for the setting, and keep a person between the tool and anyone vulnerable.

risks.title: Human review becomes a formality
risks.description: The person meant to check outputs accepts them without looking, because volume is high or the tool is usually right.
risks.treatment: Size the review to the volume, rotate reviewers, and measure how often they change an output.

risks.title: The system acts without a person approving
risks.description: An agent or automation sends, changes, or deletes something that should have waited for a person.
risks.treatment: Limit what it may do by itself to a written list, and log every action.

risks.title: There is no tested way to stop it
risks.description: When the system misbehaves, nobody knows how to stop it quickly, or the stop has never been tried.
risks.treatment: Write down the stop, name who may use it, and test it.

risks.title: People lose the skill to do the work without it
risks.description: Staff rely on the tool so far that they can no longer check it or work when it is unavailable.
risks.treatment: Keep people doing a share of the work unaided, and plan for the tool being down.

risks.title: The use grows beyond what was approved
risks.description: A tool approved for one purpose is quietly used for others, with more sensitive data or higher stakes.
risks.treatment: Ask owners to confirm the use on a schedule, and make declaring a change easy.

risks.title: Instructions hidden in content take over the tool
risks.description: Text in a document, web page, or email is treated by the model as an instruction and changes what it does.
risks.treatment: Do not give the tool authority it does not need, and treat everything it reads as untrusted.

risks.title: Credentials or keys are exposed through the tool
risks.description: API keys, passwords, or tokens are pasted into prompts, stored in notebooks, or returned in outputs.
risks.treatment: Keep secrets out of prompts, scan for them, and rotate any that are exposed.

risks.title: The tool has more access than the task needs
risks.description: An assistant or agent runs with a person's full access to files, mail, or systems.
risks.treatment: Give it its own identity with the least access that does the job.

risks.title: A model file from an unknown source is run
risks.description: Weights or code downloaded from a public site carry malicious code or hidden behavior.
risks.treatment: Take models from known sources, record the checksum, and prefer formats that cannot carry code.

risks.title: The tool is used to do something it should not
risks.description: Someone uses an approved tool to get around a control, such as extracting data they could not otherwise export.
risks.treatment: Log use, and review the logs when access rules change.

risks.title: A supplier changes its terms
risks.description: The supplier changes how it handles data, what it charges, or what it allows, with little notice.
risks.treatment: Keep the agreement on file with its notice period, and review it before it renews.

risks.title: A model or service is withdrawn
risks.description: A supplier retires a model or product that work depends on.
risks.treatment: Know what depends on each model, and keep a tested alternative for anything critical.

risks.title: Critical work depends on one supplier
risks.description: There is no alternative if the supplier fails, raises prices, or is no longer permitted.
risks.treatment: Identify the work that could not continue, and keep a fallback for it.

risks.title: A supplier has a security breach
risks.description: Data held by a supplier is exposed through a breach at the supplier.
risks.treatment: Limit what is sent, require prompt notice in the agreement, and know what each supplier holds.

risks.title: A tool is used with no agreement in place
risks.description: Staff sign up to a tool themselves, under consumer terms the organization has not agreed to.
risks.treatment: Offer an approved alternative, and make it easier to find than the unapproved one.

risks.title: AI-assisted results are reported without verification
risks.description: Analysis, code, or text produced with AI goes into a paper or report without independent checking.
risks.treatment: Require verification before publication, and record who did it.

risks.title: AI use is not disclosed where a publisher or funder requires it
risks.description: A manuscript or application uses AI in a way the journal or funder asks to be declared, and it is not.
risks.treatment: Check the publisher's and funder's rules at the start, and keep a note of what was used.

risks.title: Results cannot be reproduced
risks.description: The model version, prompts, or settings were not recorded, so the work cannot be repeated.
risks.treatment: Record the model, its version or checksum, the prompts, and the settings with the results.

risks.title: Confidential material under review is given to a tool
risks.description: A manuscript or grant under peer review is entered into an AI tool, against the reviewer's obligations.
risks.treatment: Tell reviewers plainly that this is not allowed, and offer no tool for it.

risks.title: It is unclear who owns the output
risks.description: Rights in generated text, code, or images are uncertain, or the output reproduces someone else's protected work.
risks.treatment: Check the license of the tool and the model, and review outputs meant for publication.

risks.title: Nobody is accountable for a tool in use
risks.description: A tool is in use with no named owner, so nobody answers for it or notices when it changes.
risks.treatment: Give every use a named owner, and ask them to confirm it on a schedule.

risks.title: AI is in use that the organization does not know about
risks.description: Groups adopt tools without telling anyone, so risks cannot be seen or managed.
risks.treatment: Make registering easy, and ask each unit to attest that its list is complete.

risks.title: Something goes wrong and is not reported
risks.description: People do not know how to report a problem, or fear blame, so the same failure repeats.
risks.treatment: Make reporting simple, thank people for it, and share what was learned.

risks.title: Usage costs rise without anyone noticing
risks.description: Metered use of a model grows faster than expected, or a loop runs unattended.
risks.treatment: Set a budget and an alert for each metered service.

risks.title: A legal or contractual obligation is missed
risks.description: A use falls under a rule, a contract term, or a funder's condition that nobody identified.
risks.treatment: Have the request form ask the questions that reveal the obligation, and route those to legal review.

risks.title: The one person who understands it leaves
risks.description: A locally built model or pipeline is understood by one person, who moves on.
risks.treatment: Keep a model card and a runbook with the record, and name a second person.
